short_scenes.name: Volt
short_scenes.narration: At a junction, current splits into many wires. How do engineers know how much goes where?
Watch this node. Five plus three amperes in, two plus six out. What goes in always comes out.

short_scenes.name: Volt
short_scenes.narration: A junction is just a point of wire. It can't store charge. So every bit of current that arrives must leave, like cars at a roundabout: none can disappear.

short_scenes.name: Volt
short_scenes.narration: Charge can't pile up at a point. That one rule even powers the RCCB that protects your home.

short_scenes.name: Volt
short_scenes.say: Watch the full video: Kirchhoff's current law!
short_scenes.narration: For the detailed explanation, watch the full video on our channel. It's part of our complete Network Theory course.
